analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 18, 2026)
key_insights: JPM Market Intelligence is Tactically Bullish and likes owning stocks into year-end. NVDA's print helps the market past the latest 'Wall of Worry', but it may take a few more days to convince buyers to leave the sidelines because the long-term NVDA outlook was not resolved and investors may use up-days to cut positions further.

Pre-market on Nov 18: NVDA +3.4%, Semis +2.8%, Memory +3.5%, Software +1%. Mag7 are all higher except AAPL, with GOOG and TSLA up more than 1%. Cyclicals lead Defensives, with HC and Staples lower. Bond yields are flat to down 2bp as the curve flattens and the USD stays bid.
Commodities are weaker across all three complexes, with gold down 2.1% and silver down 3.4%. WTI is below $85/bbl, which the desk attributes mostly to supply/demand dynamics rather than geopolitics.

Harlan Sur: NVDA's F3Q results and F4Q guide came in about 5% above consensus and about 1% above the buyside expectations he had heard. NVDA raised its FY28 revenue growth outlook to about 75% Y/Y from about 70%, which implies total revenue near $741B, about 6% above consensus. He keeps Overweight and raises his PT to $230 from $215.

Vera Rubin added about $20B of revenue in its first full quarter of shipments, the fastest product ramp in NVDA's history, and pulled forward the reacceleration in hyperscale business by a quarter. Management reaffirmed F4Q as the gross margin trough (71-72%) with FY28 at 72-73%.

NVDA leadership: the Board confirmed Jensen Huang will not be reinstated and the search for a permanent CEO is underway. Interim CEO Colette Kress says the roadmap is on track, with Vera Rubin Ultra next year and Feynman in 2028.

Sur's open issues on NVDA: Hopper shipments to China are halted and China is excluded from the outlook, but regulatory probes (SEC, DoJ) are likely to extend beyond China. Management did not clearly address financing and data-center buildout risk for CY28. Execution risk is elevated during a leadership transition. He expects shares to stay highly volatile near term.

Doug Anmuth: NVDA says cloud industry backlog rose to $2.5T from $2T three months ago, hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated for a sixth straight quarter, and compute is fully utilized at every hyperscaler and neocloud. GPU rental prices are rising and all buyers get the same pricing, with new pricing in the new year as supply costs rise.

Anmuth sees META with the biggest positive change in NVDA's disclosures (Muse agent passed 10M setups in its first 6 weeks, wider use of Vera Rubin stack), and GOOGL as a dual-track winner pairing NVDA racks with internal TPUs. He calls the AMZN readthrough more indirect because AWS was not named among live Vera Rubin NVL72 partners.

Anmuth says SPCX is a featured NVDA customer and NVDA's #1 equity holding per its latest 13F. NVDA sends supply first to customers with land, power and buildings ready and capital in place, which favors well-capitalized buyers over smaller neoclouds. NVDA's autonomous driving toolkit is a long-term positive for UBER.

Retail sales for October surprised to the upside. Headline +0.2% m/m (JPMC 0.0%, consensus 0.1%), control group +0.6% (JPMC 0.2%, consensus 0.3%), with sizable upward revisions to prior months. Abiel Reinhart says 4Q real consumption is on track to grow over 2% q/q saar versus the JPM forecast of 1.5%.

Chris Horvers: October retail sales were +6.8% YoY (vs +6.6% in September) and core retail sales +7.5% (vs +7.3%). On a 2-year basis core was +5.1%, in line with September, with 7 of 11 categories decelerating.

Market Intel's retail sales view: the print shows consumer strength despite inflation and negative headlines. SPX EPS is tied more to nominal GDP than real GDP, so inflation is not a problem for earnings near term, but the strong consumer and tight labor markets may add hawkishness at the Fed. Inflation may be the biggest risk for 1Q27.

Factor thoughts (Manish Sinha): Momentum holding up on SPY down days signals returning confidence. AI Momentum is leading QQQ in both sell-offs and recoveries. Investors still appear to wait for NVDA earnings and the IPO before re-grossing.
JPM APAC Tech Conference: Ed Bell says he has never seen a bigger gap between corporate commentary (in line with recent months) and investor feedback (fairly universally negative).

Bear case from the Nov 16 briefing: AI/tech takes another leg lower, the incremental buyer (retail, buybacks) steps back, a hawkish Fed narrative develops with 17 Fedspeakers this week and talk of 50bp, and positioning has not purged enough (US positioning about 20th percentile, global Semis exposure 80th percentile).

Dubravko reiterates his YE26 SPX target of 8,000 (EPS $365, 21.9x), implying 8.4% upside from Friday's close. He favors long 12M momentum vs short 3M momentum, finds Low Vol less compelling, likes AI upstream after the positioning flush, and sees consumer cyclicals challenged by affordability.

Monetization Menu (Nov 16): move back toward Tech with primary exposure to Mag7 and options to play an AI rebound, prefer Cyclicals over Defensives, and keep Europe for Cyclical/Value exposure, though a USD surge could temper it.
Today's catalysts: Fed Minutes at 2pm ET, housing data at 10am ET, TIC data at 4pm ET, and earnings from LOW, P, PANW, TGT, TJX and WWD. Eurozone CPI and UK CPI/PPI are the global data.

market_movers.rationale: Harlan Sur raises his PT to $230 from $215 and keeps Overweight after F3Q results and a F4Q guide about 5% above consensus. He raised FY28 growth guidance to about 75% but flags China, financing and leadership risks.

Doug Anmuth sees META with the biggest positive change in NVDA's disclosures, citing the Muse agent passing 10M setups and expanded use of the Vera Rubin stack. He says this is early proof of returns on capex.
Google Cloud is among the first to run live Vera Rubin NVL72 racks. Anmuth says pairing NVDA racks with internal TPUs gives a margin edge since all buyers pay the same NVDA price.
Anmuth says SPCX is a featured NVDA customer with Vera Rubin racks coming online soon. NVDA's supply priority for well-capitalized buyers favors SPCX over smaller neoclouds.

NVDA's new autonomous driving tools lower the barrier for Level 4 suppliers to plug into UBER's network, which weakens the Waymo or Tesla monopoly bear case per Anmuth. The same stack also equips rivals such as Bolt.
Anmuth calls the AMZN readthrough from NVDA's print more indirect because AWS was not named among live Vera Rubin NVL72 rack partners, though it is a leading Vera CPU partner.

sector_views.rationale: Market Intel favors moving back toward Tech with Mag7 as primary exposure, and Dubravko sees an attractive entry in AI upstream after the positioning flush.
Market Intel prefers Cyclicals over Defensives as the growth narrative reboots, and likes European Cyclical/Value exposure given relative positioning and valuation.
Dubravko's long 12M vs short 3M momentum idea is effectively Tech against Energy and Defensives. Low Vol is less compelling, with Healthcare then Utilities then Staples the best spots if holding it.
Dubravko says affordability tied to oil prices, borrowing costs and housing shortages remains a headwind, but sees longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail versus Energy.
Market Intel notes Energy gains have flipped over the last month, and Dubravko's trade ideas pair Tech against Energy and Defensives.

earnings_insights: NVDA F3Q results, reported 11/17: F4Q guide about 5% above consensus expectations and about 1% above buyside expectations Harlan Sur had heard (basis as stated by JPM, no EPS or revenue dollar figure given for the quarter).
NVDA guided FY28 revenue growth to about 75% Y/Y (up from about 70% prior) off a higher FY27 base. JPM computes this implies total FY28 revenue near $741B, about 6% above consensus estimates.
NVDA Vera Rubin added about $20B of revenue in its first full quarter of shipments. F4Q gross margin is the trough at 71-72% per management, improving to 72-73% in FY28.
NVDA halted licensed Hopper shipments to China and excluded China from its outlook. JPM says regulatory overhang is not resolved.
Upcoming earnings today (11/18, results not yet reported): LOW, P, PANW, TGT, TJX, WWD. Later this week: INTU, KEYS, ROAD, ROST, WMT, WSM on 11/19 and BMNR, CPRT, IESC, VEEV on 11/20.
Market Intel says profit margins near record levels suggest cost pass-through is not a problem for SPX earnings near term.

trade_ideas.description: Long 12M Momentum vs short 3M Momentum (Dubravko), essentially Tech versus Energy and Defensives
trade_ideas.rationale: Dubravko's factor view into year-end, consistent with the Tech washout nearing completion.

trade_ideas.description: AI Upstream attractive entry (Dubravko), with hyperscalers having medium-term room to re-rate higher
trade_ideas.rationale: The positioning flush has created an attractive entry point, and tighter compute capacity should help pricing power, margins and operating cash flow.
trade_ideas.risk: Hyperscalers have less upside near term, and the capex curve may be limited.

trade_ideas.description: Primary exposure to Mag7, with options to play a rebound in AI themes (Monetization Menu, Nov 16)
trade_ideas.rationale: Moving back toward Tech makes sense with earnings, capital markets events and the JPM APAC Tech Conference as catalysts.
trade_ideas.risk: Market may be patient and wait for catalysts. NVDA failing to reassure on AI ecosystem financing or a leg lower in AI/Tech.

trade_ideas.description: Cyclicals over Defensives, with European Cyclical/Value exposure over US counterparts (Monetization Menu)
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth narrative reboots and Europe offers relatively lower positioning and valuation.
trade_ideas.risk: Another surge in the USD may temper European outperformance, and a more hawkish Fed.

trade_ideas.description: If keeping Low Vol exposure, favor Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples (Dubravko)

risk_factors: AI/Tech takes another leg lower if NVDA fails to reassure on ecosystem financing, capital markets events are delayed, or there are negative pre-announcements at the APAC Tech Conference.
Decline in the incremental buyer: retail dip buying and buybacks could be held back if another AI/Tech downdraft occurs.
Hawkish Fed narrative: hot retail sales, 17 Fedspeakers this week, and possible talk of 50bp, which would challenge the pricing of 4 hikes.
Inflation may be the biggest risk for 1Q27, and import/export prices printed above expectations.
Positioning has not purged enough: US positioning around the 20th percentile and global Semis exposure at the 80th percentile.
NVDA regulatory overhang beyond China, including SEC and DoJ probes, and open CEO succession.
NVDA execution risk (annual product cadence, supply chain scaling, talent retention) and unaddressed CY28 financing and data-center buildout risk.
Rising compute costs pressure cloud margins and capital intensity.
A further surge in the USD could temper European outperformance.
Corporate commentary versus investor feedback gap at the JPM APAC Tech Conference.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 23.65 at the time of writing.
JPM Equity Derivatives notes NVDA options flows have shifted from downside protection to playing for earnings surprises, with little fear of another downdraft.
Hedge funds have been sellers for 6 consecutive weeks, a Positioning Intel record, and JPM expects stabilization to be led by HFs returning.

Aggregate US positioning is about the 20th percentile in the Tactical Positioning Monitor (data back to 2015), and global Semis exposure is at the 80th percentile, so there is room for another downdraft. There has not been a definitive positioning purge.
Momentum factor (JPMPURE) held up on SPY down days, and AI Momentum leads QQQ in both sell-offs and recoveries.
Low Vol factor moved from the 0th to the 25th percentile and is less attractive unless recession risk rises.
JPM recession basket (JPRECES) is +15.8% QTD versus SPX -1.2%.
JPM's EU trading desk is skewed as net sellers despite a positive APAC session.
Market Intel suggests using options to play an AI rebound and would consider US Memory and Semis plays via options.
geopolitical: NVDA halted licensed Hopper shipments to China and excluded China from its outlook. JPM says ongoing investigations are likely to extend beyond China given the focus on diversion.
SEC and DoJ probes of NVDA are cited as headline and regulatory risks.
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027 (NBC), per the political catalyst calendar.
APEC Economic Leaders Meeting in Shenzhen, China on Nov 18-19.
US Government funding deadline on Dec 11 (The Hill), and G20 Summit in Miami on Dec 15-16.
WTI below $85/bbl is attributed mostly to supply/demand dynamics rather than geopolitics.

tension_points.theme: AI tech rebound vs leg lower
tension_points.bull_case: NVDA's print and guide reassure on AI demand, capital markets events trade well, HFs who sold for 6 straight weeks return, and positioning is cleaner. NVDA options flows shifted from downside protection to earnings upside.
tension_points.bear_case: NVDA fails to reassure on AI ecosystem financing, capital markets events are delayed, or negative pre-announcements emerge at the APAC Tech Conference. Investors may use up-days to reduce positions, and US positioning at about the 20th percentile with Semis exposure at the 80th percentile shows no definitive purge.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NVDA failing to reassure on AI ecosystem financing, a delay to the expected capital markets events, or negative pre-announcements at the JPM APAC Tech Conference.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong consumer and nominal GDP growth support SPX EPS, and JPM thinks it highly unlikely the Fed moves to hike 50bp in December.
tension_points.bear_case: A hotter retail sales print, tight labor markets and 17 Fedspeakers this week, with possible talk of 50bp, could break the idea that the hiking cycle is as shallow as the current pricing of 4 hikes. Equity resilience to higher yields last week should not be the norm.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed move to hike by 50bp in December, which JPM says would create a tactical headwind to the equity bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: F4Q guide about 5% above consensus, FY28 growth raised to about 75%, Vera Rubin ramp, and gross margin trough in F4Q at 71-72%.
tension_points.bear_case: CEO search, China and regulatory probes (SEC, DoJ), unaddressed CY28 financing and data-center buildout risk, and execution risk keep shares highly volatile near term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management not clearly addressing financing and data-center buildout risk for CY28, with customer land, power and shell readiness gating allocation.
